title: BAHR & Legora: Building the firm of the future
author: Legora

dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: The source accepts the human-led, work-redesign proposition and adds a concrete organisational case: BAHR reports embedding Legora into daily practice, chaining functions across workflow stages, accelerating initial analysis and reallocating lawyer time toward deeper analysis, strategy and client outcomes. Its evidence is self-reported and promotional, however, and does not address verification, comparative performance or whether adoption produces measurable firm-wide value.
qs: By linking different steps of the platform, lawyers can streamline tasks that once took much longer.
And just that, releasing time for in-depth analysis and finding solutions, is a very big gain.” Beyond speed, it also sharpens the precision of their work.

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: BAHR’s account supports the cluster’s distinction between deployment and realised outcomes: it attributes adoption to organisational culture, tool selection and integration into everyday work, while offering no quantified evidence of productivity, accuracy or client benefits. It reinforces the need for implementation readiness beyond software availability, though it provides limited evidence on training or selected high-value workflows.
qs: Our collaboration with BAHR demonstrates how a unified culture, world-class legal minds, and cutting-edge AI can work together to shape the future of legal services.
Caroline Brochmann Byhring, Senior Associate at BAHR, puts it simply: “Legora is an integrated part of most of the tasks I do every single day.”

kp.k: BAHR selected Legora after comparative study
kp.d: In Legora’s customer story, BAHR partner Svein Gerhard Simonnaes says the firm conducted a careful study before recommending that the partnership switch to Legora. The document does not provide the study’s criteria, alternatives, sample, or measured results.
qs: “We did a very careful study and came back to the partnership saying that, look, we have Legora. It wins hands down. Let’s switch to Legora.”

kp.k: BAHR reports widespread, intensive AI adoption
kp.d: Managing Partner Thomas K. Svensen reports that 80% of BAHR personnel are active Legora users and that up to 30% use it more than ten times daily. The customer profile states that BAHR joined Legora in November 2024, has more than 250 employees, and covers 19 practice areas; the document presents no additional measurement methodology or observation period for the usage figures.
qs: “Today as much as 80% of our people are active users, and as high as 30% use Legora more than ten times a day.”

kp.k: AI is integrated into lawyers’ everyday tasks
kp.d: Senior Associate Caroline Brochmann Byhring describes Legora as integrated into most tasks she performs each day, indicating broad workflow incorporation rather than occasional or experimental use. Head of Digital Innovation Joachim Edin characterises the firm’s current adoption as only the beginning of a continuing AI programme.
qs: “Legora is an integrated part of most of the tasks I do every single day.”
“The AI journey at BAHR has already been great and we’ve achieved a lot, including world class adoption. But for us, that’s only the beginning.”

kp.k: Faster analysis reallocates time to deeper work
kp.d: Simonnaes says Legora enables analysis to be completed quickly, releasing lawyer time for more in-depth analysis and solution-finding. This is a customer-reported account of task acceleration and augmentation; the document provides no quantified time savings or comparative performance data.
qs: “We can get analysis done very quickly and move on from there. And just that, releasing time for in-depth analysis and finding solutions, is a very big gain.”

kp.k: Chained tools create new legal workflows
kp.d: Senior Digital Innovation Consultant Siok Lim says BAHR links multiple Legora functions—including tabular review, prompting, and translation—into chained workflows. The claim identifies multi-step workflow integration as a mechanism for streamlining legal tasks and enabling additional uses.
qs: “It allows us to chain together different steps of the Legora platform, for example, tabular review, prompts, and translation. And that has allowed us to unlock many new possibilities.”

kp.k: BAHR links AI tools to competitiveness
kp.d: Simonnaes frames access to strong technology as necessary for talented lawyers to work and for BAHR to compete. Svensen similarly presents Legora as one component of the firm’s future-facing organisational development, reflecting BAHR leaders’ strategic view rather than a market-wide finding.
qs: “It’s really about making sure that good people have the best tools available. Otherwise, we can’t work and we can’t compete.”
“At BAHR, we are not afraid of change. We’re building the firm for the future, and Legora is part of that machinery.”

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: BAHR speakers describe Legora as embedded in everyday legal work, with widespread and frequent use.
pts.d: Managing Partner Thomas K. Svensen reports that as much as 80% of BAHR's people are active users and as high as 30% use Legora more than ten times daily. Senior Associate Caroline Brochmann Byhring describes integration into most of her daily tasks. These are claims about adoption and use, rather than measured improvements in legal outcomes.

pts.k: AI speeds initial analysis and frees lawyers to undertake deeper analysis and find solutions; Legora also claims improved precision.
pts.d: Partner Svein Gerhard Simonnaes attributes a substantial gain to completing analysis quickly and reallocating time to deeper work. Legora's editorial narrative additionally claims sharper precision and greater focus on strategy, creativity and client outcomes. The account describes augmentation of lawyers' work, not replacement of lawyers or direct reliance on autonomous output.

pts.k: Chaining platform functions changes legal workflows and streamlines previously time-consuming tasks.
pts.d: Senior Digital Innovation Consultant Siok Lim describes connecting tabular review, prompts and translation to create additional workflow possibilities. Legora characterizes this as streamlining tasks that previously took longer. Neither identifies particular matters or quantifies the time savings.

pts.k: BAHR presents access to strong tools as necessary for competitiveness and AI adoption as the beginning of continued firm development.
pts.d: Simonnaes frames equipping good people with the best tools as essential to working and competing. Svensen presents Legora as part of building BAHR for the future, while Head of Digital Innovation Joachim Edin describes existing adoption as only a beginning. These are strategic expectations without a specific forecast of employment, revenue, pricing or market-share changes.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered is a vendor-published customer account combining reported usage figures, practitioner experience and an unspecified internal product comparison.
pts.d: Svensen supplies the usage percentages, but the document gives no measurement period, active-user definition or collection methodology. Byhring, Simonnaes and Lim supply firsthand accounts of task integration, time release and workflow functionality. Simonnaes says BAHR conducted a careful study before choosing Legora, but no comparator products, criteria or results are disclosed. The precision and client-outcome claims have no separate supporting measurements or case examples, and no independent evaluation is presented.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Reported benefits concern current use in the 2025 account following BAHR's November 2024 joining date; future development has no specified horizon.
pts.d: The source lists BAHR as joining Legora in November 2024 and describes usage and workflow benefits as present-day experience. It does not give an exact observation date or duration. Future-facing statements are open-ended. Legora frames the benefits as arising when capable lawyers and AI tools are combined with a unified culture receptive to change; workflow gains specifically involve linking platform steps.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The direct subjects are BAHR's lawyers and wider personnel; firm competitiveness and client outcomes are presented as downstream beneficiaries.
pts.d: The profile describes BAHR as having 250+ employees and 19 practice areas. The usage figures refer to its 'people,' not expressly only lawyers. Lawyers are described as gaining faster analysis, connected workflows and more time for deeper thinking, strategy and creativity. Digital innovation staff describe configuring workflows, and firm leadership links tools to competitiveness. Clients are mentioned as intended beneficiaries of greater focus on outcomes, but no client-specific results are reported. The account makes no concrete claim about profession-wide displacement or public access to justice.
